input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: Using `all` suppresses the entire positional arguments section when any argument lacks help. The section should appear when at least one argument is documented.
- rationale: For a command with one argument whose help is set and another whose help is None, this condition is false, so even the documented argument disappears from help. The empty-description fallback is never reached for the mixed case it is intended to support.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: `all` is used where `any` is needed in the guard. It also describes the same consequence, where a mix of documented and undocumented arguments suppresses the whole section and drops the documented one. It does not mention the empty-args case, but the core mechanism matches.
